title: Occupation-selective photon-pair interactions in a flux-pumped SQUID resonator
authors: L. N. Ferreira, D. Z. Rossatto, A. S. M. de Castro, G. D. de Moraes Neto
abstract: Flux-pumped Josephson circuits provide a versatile platform for parametric photon generation and multimode bosonic control. We identify an occupation-conditioned pair interaction that arises when two harmonic normal modes participate in the same driven SQUID coordinate. We consider a degenerate pair process in which two photons are created or annihilated in a signal mode while the occupation of a second harmonic mode remains unchanged. Although it does not exchange excitations, this controller mode modifies both the resonance frequency and the strength of the pair transition. The two effects have different physical origins: diagonal Josephson nonlinearities shift the pair resonance, whereas the nonlinear Josephson matrix element makes the avoided-crossing gap itself depend on the controller occupation. Starting from the full Josephson cosine, we develop complementary time-dependent Schrieffer--Wolff and Magnus descriptions that expose the direct and virtual processes responsible for this interaction, and benchmark the resulting effective theory against a numerically converged Floquet treatment of the unexpanded two-mode circuit Hamiltonian. The occupation dependence produces a two-dimensional pair spectrum that enables selective transitions within the bosonic Fock lattice. When the controller is prepared in a coherent superposition, the same interaction converts this conditional dynamics into signal--controller entanglement and controller-dependent non-Gaussian state generation. Observable-level comparisons further show that the variation of the pair-transition strength cannot be reproduced by occupation-dependent resonance shifts alone. These results establish a boson-controlled parametric interaction in which the state of one harmonic mode controls both the spectral position and the coupling strength of a nonlinear process in another.
summary: This paper analyzes an occupation-conditioned pair interaction in flux-pumped Josephson circuits, treating the system as two coupled bosonic modes. Using advanced perturbation theory, the authors show that the state of one mode can simultaneously control both the resonance frequency and the coupling strength of a nonlinear process in a second mode. This establishes a powerful mechanism for boson-controlled parametric interactions leading to entanglement.
main_problem: The paper identifies and characterizes an occupation-conditioned pair interaction occurring in a system where two bosonic modes share a driven Josephson coordinate.
main_result: The interaction is a boson-controlled parametric process where the state of one mode controls both the spectral position and the coupling strength of a nonlinear process in the other mode.
method: The authors developed complementary analytical descriptions using time-dependent Schrieffer–Wolff and Magnus expansions, benchmarking the effective theory against a full Floquet treatment.
model_or_system: The physical platform is a flux-pumped Josephson circuit, modeled by a two-mode Hamiltonian derived from the full Josephson cosine, allowing for parametric photon generation and multimode bosonic control.
key_observables: Two-dimensional pair spectrum, signal-controller entanglement, and the variation of the pair-transition strength.
important_parameters: Normal-mode frequencies, pump frequency ($\Omega$), and the occupation number ($n_b$) of the controller mode.
main_assumptions: The analysis uses the weak-pump regime for analytical derivations, and the zero-point phases are treated as representative circuit-level parameters.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the physical mechanism, showing how virtual corrections from off-resonant processes contribute to the occupation-dependent resonance positions and pair-transition strengths.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical platform (flux-pumped SQUID) to identifying the specific interaction (occupation-conditioned pair process), detailing the two distinct physical origins of the conditioning (resonance shift vs. gap change), and finally applying the theory to entanglement generation.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical framework for realizing and controlling nonlinear parametric interactions in superconducting circuits, which is highly relevant to quantum optics and cavity QED.
